findings.evidence: Keep a short ranked set (five to ten by default), one template row per candidate; adoption cost covers setup, workflow switch, permissions and trust.
findings.fix: Remove the column restatement in the prose because the template on lines 18-25 already lists the columns. Keep only the parts the template cannot show: the default of five to ten candidates, the strategic-bet rule and the tier and priority labels.

findings.evidence: Then read shipped features, unreleased or flagged work, issues and support feedback, research and telemetry, applying the Gotchas below.
findings.fix: Add a checkpoint after Baseline so the process has more than the single final check in step 5. Before Discover, write a short baseline table with columns live, built-but-unreleased, planned and unknown, each row citing its source. Discover may use only the live and unknown rows, which keeps flagged or stale-roadmap items out of the candidate list.

findings.evidence: ## NEVER (two items: trend features without mechanism, parity features as 10x)
findings.fix: Add one more NEVER item with its reason, drawn from a known failure in this domain, for example: 'NEVER put an idea in Do Now when its only evidence is request volume from one account or segment: loud accounts dominate tickets, and the work ships to an audience that does not use it.'

findings.evidence: Use when users ask what to build next, want a product to be substantially more valuable, ask for '10x' ideas, growth levers or small wins
findings.fix: Find and rank high-leverage product opportunities from repository, feedback and usage evidence, saved as a strategy session file. Use when users ask what to build next, want a product to be substantially more valuable, ask for '10x' ideas, growth levers or small wins, worry about churn, retention or users not coming back, or ask whether a requested feature is the right next move, even if they never say 'strategy'. Gives recommendations and assumptions to validate only; not for implementing code, sprint plans, user stories, effort estimates, competitor or pricing research, or committed-date roadmaps.

findings.evidence: Negatives are terse, context-free prompts such as "compare competitor pricing for our SaaS" and "brainstorm names for our new mobile app"
findings.fix: Rewrite at least four should-not-trigger queries as realistic near-misses that include file paths and personal context. Example: 'our PM approved the 10x session's Do Now item (shared challenges) - break it into user stories with acceptance criteria in docs/stories.md'. Another example: 'pull our churn numbers from reports/usage.csv and chart them by cohort for the board deck'.

findings.evidence: tier them **Massive Gems**, **Medium Gems** and **Small Gems**
findings.fix: Define each tier by a test the agent can apply, not by feel. Massive: removes a whole step of the user's job or unlocks a new user group. Medium: removes friction in a step that is used often. Small: a fix of days or less to one known pain point. When an idea fits two tiers, put it in the lower one.

findings.evidence: If a matching `<product-slug>/10x/` folder exists, read its latest session first
findings.fix: State how to derive the slug and how to resolve a mismatch. List the folders under .claude/docs/ai/ first. Reuse an existing folder whose prior session names the same product, even if the slug differs from the repo name (for example 'Habitlane' resolves to habit-tracker/). Only when none matches, create a kebab-case slug from the product name.
